policy.last_change: 4 Mar 2026 (-25bp, eff. 5 Mar); held 9 Apr and 6 May

policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 7 May close (1x4 3.88, 3x6 4.02, 6x9 4.24, 9x12 4.41 vs WIBOR 3M 3.84) price roughly 55bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 6 May (core probably rose in April; wait-and-see); Glapiński (7 May): the probability of a hike has risen and a cut is very unlikely - a CPI breach of 3.5% with persistent forecasts would trigger action. Dąbrowski (30 Apr): the chance of cuts fell sharply after the April CPI. April flash CPI 3.2% (30 Apr; 3.0% expected); core 2.7% in March. The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 15 May.
policy.risk_text: Glapiński (7 May) moved to hike risk: a CPI breach of 3.5% with persistent forecasts would trigger action - May CPI (29 May) and the July projection are the tests. The front end trades oil and the Iran talks; long end: heavy May supply.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after March PLN 69.6bn (25.6% of the limit); the fiscal notification and the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) to 15 May.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~49% (after 28 Apr, MoF) financed; budget accounts ~PLN 184bn at end-April (MoF estimate). S&P reviews Poland on 8 May (A-, stable; Erste sees a sizeable risk of a negative outlook); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 6 May; April CPI 3.2% y/y; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 4.1%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 7 May: Glapiński: the probability of a hike has risen since April and a cut is very unlikely; a CPI breach of the 3.5% band with persistent forecasts, or projections making it unavoidable, would trigger action; core is rising but demand and wages are subdued; Pekao called it hawkish, ING wait-and-see; FRAs price ~2 hikes by year-end vs >3 early in the week (XTB); MoF offers PLN 3-6bn of 46-week bills on 8 May. Abroad: Iran was still reviewing the US memorandum; Brent ~$97-100; the CNB held at 3.50% (7-0), Norges Bank hiked; ~50bp of ECB and BoE hikes priced; UST 10Y ~4.35%, Bund 3.00%; Trump gave the EU until 4 July to cut tariffs.

calendar.plan_text: MoF May plan (30 Apr): sale auctions on 13 May (PLN 6-12bn), 21 May (7-13bn) and 27 May (6-12bn) in OK0129 (new 2Y, replaces OK0128), NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; a 46-week T-bill on 8 May (3-6bn); no switch. ~49% of 2026 needs financed after the April sales.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining May sales: 13 May, 21 May, 27 May. Next MPC 1-2 Jun: a hold is expected; the July projection is the next marker.

facts.core_text: Regime: deal hopes versus stalemate - oil swinging around $100-110; the NBP held at 3.75% on 6 May while FRAs price roughly 55bp of NBP hikes; the ECB is priced for a June hike, the BoE for hikes, the Fed has turned to hike risk, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 51bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 261bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 7 May close). CNB holds 7-0; Brent below $100 (7 May).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK sold PLN 0.69bn on 29 Apr plus 0.13bn additional (demand 0.94bn); next FPC tenders 14 and 28 May; the FWSZ 2026 bond plan was raised to PLN 76.6bn.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
